instruction: I want to listen to the song from this video without watching it. Convert the video "Baby Justin Bieber.mp4" from the desktop to audio format and save it as "Baby Justin Bieber.mp3" on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires converting video to audio using VLC with natural language instruction. Evaluator checks file exists with minimum 50KB size (lower threshold to allow for various encoding settings).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file creation at the specified path (/home/user/Desktop/Baby Justin Bieber.mp3)
Getter logic is sound: uses bash stat command to check file existence and extract size
Metric comparison logic correctly checks both file existence and minimum size requirement (50KB)
Data flow is correct: getter extracts file properties, metric compares against expected minimum size
However, evaluator does NOT verify actual MP3 format/codec - only checks file extension and size
A file with .mp3 extension but wrong codec (WAV, OGG, etc.) would incorrectly pass verification
No verification of audio content quality, duration, or whether audio actually came from the video
Minimum size threshold of 50KB is very lenient and could allow corrupted/incomplete conversions
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add file format verification using 'file' command or audio metadata inspection to ensure it's actually MP3
Consider checking audio duration to verify conversion completeness (should be similar to video duration)
Optionally verify audio codec/bitrate using ffprobe or similar tool to ensure proper MP3 encoding
Consider increasing minimum size threshold or making it dependent on source video duration
